sourceCopy.name: RMD Calculator
sourceCopy.title: RMD Calculator 2026 Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Estimate a 2026 RMD with the IRS Uniform Lifetime Table. Free, no account, and calculated in your browser.
sourceCopy.intro: Estimate an illustrative 2026 required minimum distribution (RMD) from an account balance and age. The table, balance year, and calculation are shown.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: How do I estimate a 2026 required minimum distribution?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: Divide the eligible account balance from December 31, 2025 by the IRS Uniform Lifetime Table factor for your age in 2026. This calculator applies Table III only and does not decide whether an RMD is due.
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. The calculation runs in this browser. The balance and age you enter are not uploaded or saved by this tool.
howTo: Enter the eligible account balance as of December 31, 2025.
Enter the age you will reach during 2026.
Calculate to see the Table III factor, formula, and illustrative amount; check that this table applies to your account.

example.label: Load IRS example: $100,000 balance and age 75

fields.balanceDateNote: Use the balance from December 31 of the previous year: 2025 for this 2026 estimate.
fields.ageDateNote: Use your age on your birthday in 2026. Age 120 represents age 120 and over in Table III.
fields.accuracyNote: U.S. estimate using IRS Publication 590-B (2025), Appendix B, Table III, for 2026. It does not determine whether or when you must take a distribution. It does not cover inherited accounts or the separate table for a sole spouse beneficiary more than 10 years younger. Plan rules and other exceptions may change the amount. Verify with your plan custodian or a qualified tax professional. Not tax or financial advice.
fields.tableNote: Source and scope: IRS Publication 590-B (2025), Appendix B, Table III. The IRS example rounds $100,000 ÷ 24.6 to about $4,065; this display keeps cents.

messages.checkInputs: Enter a balance from 0 to 1 trillion and a whole age from 72 to 120.
messages.copyUnavailable: Copy is not available in this browser.

additionalFaqs.question: What balance and age does a 2026 RMD estimate use?
additionalFaqs.answer: For this illustration, enter the account balance from December 31, 2025 and your age on your birthday in 2026. IRS rules and account type determine which table and timing apply.

additionalFaqs.question: Can I use this for an inherited IRA or a much younger spouse?
additionalFaqs.answer: Not reliably. Inherited accounts may use different rules and tables. A sole spouse beneficiary more than 10 years younger generally uses the Joint Life and Last Survivor Table, not Table III.

additionalFaqs.question: Does this tell me when or whether I must take an RMD?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. It only divides a balance by a Table III factor. It does not determine your required beginning date, eligibility, deadlines, aggregation rules, plan exceptions, or tax consequences.
